title: Failover Credit Arbitration and SLA Clauses for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Produce a single, review-ready artifact that defines SLA metrics for dedicated capacity customers, the error-budget math, and a deterministic arbitration process for issuing credits when multiple failure modes overlap (e.g., regional outage + autoscale failure). The artifact should include example contract language, measurable SLIs, and an operational playbook for detection, customer notification, and credit issuance.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect contractual throughput commitments and predictable remediation when service does not meet those commitments. Prior artifacts at Redwood focus on throughput guarantees and credit formulas, but lack a deterministic arbitration layer for complex multi-failure scenarios and clear language for mix-and-match entitlements (sustained vs burstable capacity). This ticket consolidates those gaps into one canonical spec for legal, sales, and eng to review.
objectives: Define SLIs and per-customer measurement windows for dedicated throughput commitments
Specify a numeric error-budget policy and credit computation that is simple to audit
Create an arbitration algorithm to determine how credits are applied when multiple SLA classes or failure causes overlap
Draft contract-ready language (clauses) and acceptance criteria for the legal and sales teams
Publish an operational playbook for detection, notification, remediation, and postmortem credit reconciliation
sla_definitions: SLA classes: (1) Sustained Throughput Commitment (STC): customer-committed aggregate inference throughput measured in successful token-processing capacity over a 30-day rolling window. (2) Burstable Headroom (BH): short-duration peak capacity (measured per 1-hour windows) allowed above STC for transient traffic spikes. (3) Availability Floor (AF): percentage of successful request completions within 300ms P50 and 1s P95 for standard model families. Each SLA includes a baseline measurement window and an entitlement value expressed in normalized serve-units (SU). Example: Customer STC = 100k SU/day, BH = 10k SU/hour, AF = 99.5% for P95 latency. The spec ties SU to tokens/sec * weighted model factor to account for model heterogeneity.
measurement_methodology: Primary measurement source is the Redwood telemetry pipeline aggregated per-customer and per-deployment zone. Measurements use the following windows: STC measured over rolling 30d calendar window, BH measured over rolling 7d with hourly bucketing, AF measured daily and reported on 30d rolling aggregates. Successful SU is defined as token emissions not interrupted by runtime exceptions and not served from client-side retries. Timestamps use UTC and are tagged by AZ/region. All SLIs are computed from the authoritative time-series (metrics.redwood-inference.prod) and archived for 1 year for auditability.
error_budget_policy: Each SLA class has an error budget defined as: EB = 1 - SLA_target. For example, AF SLA_target=99.5% => EB=0.5% over the 30-day window. For throughput SLAs, budget is the proportion of committed SU not delivered: EB_throughput = 1 - (served_SU / committed_SU) over the measurement window. If EB for any SLA class is exhausted for two consecutive windows, the system escalates and the customer becomes eligible for credits as described below. Credits are capped at 100% of monthly committed fees for the relevant capacity block.
credit_arbitration_rules: When a service disruption could trigger multiple SLA credit events (e.g., an AZ hardware failure causes both AF violations and STC under-delivery, and autoscaler failed to add nodes), credits are computed deterministically as follows: (1) Compute per-SLA raw credit amounts independently using the credit formula in section 'contract_language_snippet'. (2) Classify each raw credit as primary (directly tied to paid entitlement: STC/BH) or ancillary (availability, latency). (3) Apply arbitration: if primary credit exists, apply primary credit first up to its cap. Ancillary credits apply only to residual impact not already compensated. (4) If overlapping primary credits exist across multiple entitlements (e.g., both STC and BH shortfalls), prorate the customer's total credit proportional to the committed SU of each entitlement. (5) If the failure is attributable to customer misconfiguration (validated by logs and support investigation), reduce applicable credits by up to 100% depending on degree of responsibility. All arbitration decisions must be logged and exposed to the customer in the post-incident reconciliation report.
autoscale_integration_policy: Autoscaling behavior is an operational control that interacts with SLA calculations: (1) If customer's autoscale policy was set to 'conservative' (explicit config flag) and prevented expected scale-up, the arbitration flow flags this as partial-customer-responsibility. (2) If Redwood's autoscaler failed to provision capacity within configured autoscale SLAs, treat as Redwood-caused failure. (3) Autoscale success/failure events are captured as discrete telemetry events and form part of the root-cause ensemble used by arbitration. To enable fair treatment, product will surface autoscale recommendations and advisories in the Console; customers are required to opt into advisory changes for them to affect entitlement calculations.
customer_notification_playbook: 1) Detection: automated alert triggers when any SLA crosses warning thresholds. 2) Initial notice: within 30 minutes of confirmed degradation, send templated alert to customer primary contacts with summary metrics and estimated remediation ETA. 3) Status updates: every 60 minutes until resolution, with incident severity, impacted entitlements, and preliminary credit exposure estimate. 4) Post-incident: within 5 business days, provide a reconciliation report including measured SLIs, arbitration decisions, raw credit math, and remediation actions. 5) Payment/credit: credits appear on the next billing cycle as a line item; for disputes, customers may raise a support ticket and trigger a secondary audit.
contract_language_snippet: Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Dedicated Capacity in accordance with the Customer's committed entitlements. For each Billing Period, if Redwood fails to meet a Committed Throughput entitlements, Customer will be eligible for a Service Credit equal to min(Committed_Fee, Floor( (Committed_SU - Served_SU) / Committed_SU * Committed_Fee * CreditMultiplier )). 'CreditMultiplier' defaults to 0.8 for sustained throughput shortfalls and 0.5 for burstable headroom shortfalls. Service Credits for availability (AF) are computed as a percentage of the monthly dedicated fee using the table below: AF >= 99.5% -> 0% credit; 99.0%–99.49% -> 5% credit; 98.0%–98.99% -> 15% credit; <98.0% -> 30% credit. Credits resulting from concurrent failures will be applied per the Credit Arbitration Rules section; credits will in no event exceed 100% of the applicable monthly fee. Customer misconfiguration or third-party network issues attributable to Customer will reduce eligible credits proportionally as described in the arbitration policy. All credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for the failure to meet the SLA.
acceptance_criteria: Legal accepts contract snippets and markup for insertion into standard Dedicated Service Agreement
Billing can compute credits from telemetry inputs and produce line-item credit entries in the billing system for test customers
SRE can implement deterministic arbitration algorithm in playbook with reproducible inputs and produce reconciliation report for a simulated incident
Console surfaces autoscale advisory flag and shows preliminary credit exposure during incidents
At least two E2E QA incident simulations validate correct credit calculations and notification cadence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers dispute attribution leading to lengthy credit negotiations. Mitigation: provide detailed machine-readable incident reports and preserve audit logs for 1 year.

Risk: Complex arbitration causes implementation lag across billing and SRE. Mitigation: implement a reference implementation service and a test harness that both teams can run against recorded incidents.
Risk: Overly generous multipliers lead to margin erosion. Mitigation: set multiplier defaults conservatively and introduce tiered multipliers for enterprise deals with custom negotiation.
dependencies: SRE: final event taxonomy for autoscale and capacity failures
Billing: ability to accept programmatic credit entries and expose them on invoices
Legal: approval of final contract wording and limit-of-liability edits
Console UX: space to show preliminary credit exposure and autoscale advisories
